evidence.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has moved from an emerging technology to a strategic business capability that is reshaping how organizations create value, manage operations, interact with customers and make decisions. The rapid development of generative AI, large language models, machine learning and AI-enabled automation has accelerated adoption across finance, marketing, human resources, supply chains, customer service, information technology and knowledge-intensive activities. This paper examines the impact of AI on business with particular emphasis on productivity, cost efficiency, revenue generation, innovation, decision-making, customer experience, employment and organizational transformation. The study adopts a descriptive and analytical research design based primarily on secondary data from recent international reports and research publications. Evidence indicates that organizational AI adoption has risen sharply: Stanford's 2025 AI Index reported that 78% of surveyed organizations used AI in 2024, while its 2026 update reports 88% organizational adoption in 2025. At the same time, the realization of enterprise-level value remains uneven. McKinsey's 2025 research indicates that many organizations remain in experimentation or pilot stages, despite reporting use-case-level cost and revenue benefits. The paper argues that AI should not be viewed merely as a cost-reduction tool; its strategic value is greatest when organizations redesign workflows, strengthen governance, develop employee capabilities and use AI to support growth and innovation. The study concludes with recommendations for responsible AI adoption, workforce reskilling, data governance, cybersecurity and measurement of business value. Key words: Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Business Performance, Productivity, Automation, Innovation, Workforce Transformation, Digital Transformation, AI Governance 1. Introduction Artificial Intelligence refers broadly to computational systems capable of performing tasks that traditionally require human intelligence, including learning, reasoning, prediction, language processing, pattern recognition and decision support. In business, AI has evolved from specialized analytical applications into a general-purpose technology capable of influencing a wide range of organizational activities. Generative AI has further expanded this impact by enabling systems to generate text, images, software code, summaries, analyses and other forms of content. The importance of AI for business is reflected in the speed of investment and adoption. Stanford's 2025 AI Index reported that 78% of organizations surveyed were using AI in 2024, compared with 55% in 2023, while the share using generative AI in at least one business function increased from 33% to 71%. The 2026 AI Index reports that organizational AI adoption reached 88% in 2025 and that generative AI was used in at least one business function by 70% of organizations surveyed. These figures demonstrate that AI is becoming an important component of mainstream business strategy rather than remaining an experimental technology. However, adoption does not automatically translate into business value. McKinsey's 2025 research found that most organizations were still experimenting or piloting AI, with fewer having scaled it across the enterprise. The central managerial challenge is therefore shifting from whether to adopt AI to how to integrate it effectively into business processes while managing risks relating to privacy, cybersecurity, bias, intellectual property, reliability and employment. This research paper evaluates both the positive and disruptive consequences of AI and develops a framework for organizations seeking sustainable and responsible AI adoption. 2. Review of Literature 2.1 AI adoption and business transformation Stanford's AI Index provides evidence of rapid growth in corporate AI adoption and investment. The 2025 report documented record private investment in AI and a significant increase in organizational use. The 2026 AI Index further indicates that global corporate AI investment more than doubled in 2025 and that generative AI accounted for a major share of private AI funding. The evidence suggests that AI is increasingly treated as a strategic investment rather than a standalone technology project. 2.2 AI and productivity Research increasingly associates AI with productivity improvements, although the magnitude depends on task characteristics, employee capability and the degree of workflow integration. The OECD's 2025 analysis estimated that, under alternative adoption and exposure scenarios, AI could add approximately 0.4 to 1.3 percentage points to annual aggregate labour-productivity growth in highly exposed G7 economies. The OECD emphasizes that gains vary across countries because of differences in industry structure and adoption rates. 2.3 AI and the future of work The World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report 2025 highlights the dual effect of technology on employment. Based on employer expectations, 170 million jobs could be created and 92 million displaced by 2030, resulting in a net increase of 78 million jobs. The report also identifies AI, big data and cybersecurity among the rapidly growing skill areas while emphasizing that creative thinking, resilience, flexibility and other human capabilities remain important. 2.4 AI maturity and realization of value McKinsey's 2025 studies indicate that organizations are increasingly redesigning workflows, establishing AI governance and retraining employees, but many remain at an early stage of enterprise scaling. Its research also suggests that high-performing organizations tend to combine efficiency objectives with growth and innovation objectives. This supports the view that AI creates greater strategic value when it changes how work is performed rather than simply automating isolated tasks. 3. Objectives of the Study To examine the growing role of Artificial Intelligence in modern business. To analyse the impact of AI on productivity, cost efficiency and business performance. To study the influence of AI on marketing, finance, human resources, operations and customer service. To identify the opportunities created by generative AI and AI-enabled automation. To examine major risks and challenges associated with business adoption of AI. To analyse the implications of AI for employment, skills and workforce transformation. To suggest strategies for responsible, effective and sustainable AI adoption. 4. Research Methodology The study follows a descriptive and analytical research design based on secondary data. Information was collected from authoritative international reports, institutional publications and business research reports, with particular emphasis on recent evidence from 2025 and 2026. The major sources include the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (AI Index), OECD, World Economic Forum and McKinsey. The study uses comparative interpretation of reported adoption, investment, productivity and workforce indicators. The research is conceptual and evidence-based; it does not claim to establish causal relationships for individual firms. The analysis focuses on five dimensions: (1) operational efficiency, (2) revenue and customer value, (3) decision-making and innovation, (4) workforce and employment, and (5) governance and risk. Secondary data are interpreted to identify common business implications and managerial priorities. 5. Impact of AI on Major Business Functions 6.1 Finance and accounting AI can automate invoice processing, expense classification, reconciliation, fraud detection, forecasting, financial reporting and exception management. Machine learning models can identify unusual transactions, while generative AI can support document review, management reporting and natural-language analysis. These applications can reduce repetitive effort and allow finance professionals to focus on analysis, controls and business partnering. However, financial AI systems require strong audit trails, segregation of duties, data quality and human review for material decisions. 6.2 Marketing and sales AI enables customer segmentation, recommendation systems, campaign optimization, sentiment analysis, lead scoring and personalized content generation. Generative AI can accelerate the creation of marketing copy, product descriptions and campaign variants. The main strategic benefit is the ability to analyse large amounts of customer information rapidly and tailor interactions at scale. Risks include privacy violations, inappropriate personalization, biased targeting and the generation of inaccurate or misleading content. 6.3 Human resource management AI is increasingly used in recruitment support, workforce planning, learning recommendations, employee service desks and skills analysis. title: TARA: Task-Adaptive Rank Allocation for Efficient Large Language Model Fine-Tuning in Geo-Information Text Classification
abstract: Geo-information texts, including geospatial data-use regulations and Earth observation metadata, are central to data governance and compliance auditing in remote sensing ecosystems. Full fine-tuning of large pre-trained language models is often computationally impractical, while standard LoRA reduces cost but assigns a fixed rank to all adapted modules, ignoring differences across layers and projection types. This paper proposes TARA, a task-adaptive rank allocation method for LoRA-based fine-tuning. TARA assigns learnable importance scores to rank dimensions and uses Gumbel–Sigmoid sampling with the Straight-Through Estimator to learn discrete rank masks under a global sparsity constraint. We further construct RSRegulation, a geospatial regulatory compliance benchmark containing 4032 English-language samples derived from 168 clauses across seven regulatory and policy sources with clause-level data isolation. Across five random seeds, TARA achieves 95.30 ± 0.10% accuracy and 95.44 ± 0.10% F1 with a maximum trainable adapter budget of 1.57 M parameters. The learned soft allocation corresponds to approximately 0.38 M effective adapter parameters and 75.8% soft rank compression. Physical hard pruning reduces the deployed adapter to 0.086 M parameters while retaining 95.12 ± 0.11% accuracy and 95.21 ± 0.10% F1. Layer-wise analysis shows that value projections retain higher ranks than query projections under the current task and backbone, revealing a task-dependent non-uniform allocation pattern.

title: An Embodied, Affect-Driven Multi-Agent Social Simulation as a Log Generator for Computational Narrative Tasks
abstract: Computational narrative—the automatic sifting, composition and interpretation of stories—needs raw material: event logs rich enough to yield tellable stories. Social simulations are an attractive source but only if their logs are embodied, eventful and interconnected so that concurrent threads share the coordinates a telling must weave. We present a dependency-light multi-agent social simulation built to that specification as a synthetic log generator for downstream narrative tasks. Its distinguishing feature is that perception follows from position: agents encounter one another by co-location, and every event records the set of agents present to witness it. That explicit, queryable who-perceived-what relation—left disembodied or implicit by prior simulations—is what focalised composition needs, and recovering it is the gap this work addresses. Agents negotiate shared activities and exclusive relationships directly, driven by affect and per-agent temperament. Run in a calibrated, seeded free mode, social structure—couples, jealousy, affairs, break-ups—emerges unscripted from local interaction: across 150 random casts the structural invariants hold in every run, while dramatic outcomes vary widely from seed to seed, and a disjoint held-out population of 150 fresh seeds reproduces every calibrated band. A narrative-interest diagnostic instruments the logs, separating routine from active runs and reading off which dramatic configurations occur.

title: Modulations-expert: A MATLAB GUI toolbox for automatic modulation recognition and blind demodulation
abstract: Automatic modulation recognition (AMR) is an important task in non-cooperative and cognitive radio communications. This paper presents Modulations-Expert, a MATLAB-based graphical toolbox for automatic modulation recognition, dataset generation, feature extraction, visualization, feature selection, and blind demodulation of analog and digital communication signals. The toolbox integrates multiple machine learning classifiers and statistical feature extraction methods within a unified graphical environment. It also supports modulation parameter estimation and blind demodulation for several digital modulation schemes. Modulations-Expert provides a flexible and extensible platform for AMR research, evaluation, and education.

title: Challenges and opportunities of generative artificial intelligence models in audio/acoustic domain: a comprehensive survey
abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed image and text processing, but its adoption in the audio/acoustic domain remains underexplored due to inherent challenges in modeling long-term temporal dependencies in one-dimensional signals and achieving human-perceptible coherence. This comprehensive survey addresses these gaps by systematically reviewing state-of-the-art generative AI models, including generative adversarial networks (GANs), diffusion/flow-matching models, variational autoencoders (VAEs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), transformers, and Neural Codec Language Models (Codec LMs), organized around three primary application domains: (1) speech synthesis , encompassing text-to-speech conversion, neural vocoding, voice conversion, and zero-shot voice cloning; (2) music generation , covering both symbolic and acoustic composition, multi-track generation, and style transfer; and (3) general audio synthesis, sound effects, and source separation , including text-to-audio generation, audio restoration and enhancement, data augmentation, and conditional source separation. We provide a detailed taxonomy of architectures, functionalities, comparative strengths, and limitations, supported by common evaluation metrics. Structured comparisons with existing surveys demonstrate that this is the first work to jointly cover all three audio domains and all generative model families, while also providing dedicated evaluation-metric analysis and cross-domain comparative assessments. We further highlight emerging opportunities in AI applications such as healthcare monitoring (e.g., symptom analysis and mental health assessment) and biometric authentication, demonstrating the potential of synthetic audio to address real-life challenges. Through research gap identification, model efficacy comparison, and future direction outlining, this survey serves as a foundational reference for advancing generative AI techniques across the audio domain.

title: A Comprehensive Review of Large Language Models for Nanophotonics: From Surrogate Modeling to Autonomous Design
abstract: Metasurfaces have revolutionized the development of photonic devices by enabling unprecedented precision in light manipulation. However, their design processes are often constrained by computationally expensive simulations and complex high-dimensional design spaces. Although deep learning has accelerated the design process by serving as a surrogate model, it remains constrained by task-specific architectures and lacks universal reasoning capabilities. This review surveys how Large Language Models (LLMs) are adding semantic interfaces, code generation, and tool orchestration to established numerical nanophotonic workflows. We first outline the development from classical neural networks to transformer-based models and their applications in nanophotonic design. We then review the emergence of LLM-related methods in nanophotonics and organize them into two operational modes: surrogate models that treat structure-spectrum mapping as a language task, and agentic systems that have been demonstrated to generate code, orchestrate selected simulation steps, and support closed-loop optimization. Furthermore, to identify future cross-disciplinary opportunities, we briefly explore applications of LLMs in research fields such as materials science and wireless communications. This review concludes by looking ahead to the next generation of multimodal foundation models with physical perception capabilities. In this vision, artificial intelligence is evolving from passive tools into active collaborators, participating in autonomous scientific discovery.

title: Toward the Optimal Regret-Instability Trade-off in Multi-Armed Bandits
abstract: Multi-armed bandit algorithms are evaluated by regret, yet comparable regret can coexist with different allocations across independent runs. We study the trade-off between worst-case regret $\mathcal{R}_{K,T}$ and instability $\mathcal S_{K,T}$, defined as the largest standard deviation of a terminal pull count, for $K$ arms and $T$ rounds. We prove the finite-time lower bound $\mathcal R_{K,T}\mathcal S_{K,T}\ge C T^{3/2}$, where $C$ is independent of $K$ and $T$, under a finite-time regret condition and without the regularity assumptions imposed in the prior asymptotic analysis. We also introduce Stabilized Lower-Envelope UCB (\textup{\textsc{SLE-UCB}}), a new tunable algorithm combining a running lower-envelope index with a decreasing pull-count stabilizer. \textup{\textsc{SLE-UCB}} satisfies $\mathcal R_{K,T}\mathcal S_{K,T}=O(T^{3/2}\log K)$, with an implicit constant independent of $K$ and $T$, matching the lower bound exactly in $T$ and within a logarithmic factor in $K$. To prove the instability bound, we develop a new offline top-prefix representation that removes path dependence from online decisions. Together with single-reward perturbations and the Efron--Stein inequality, this representation controls pull-count variance. Thus, regret and instability depend reciprocally on $K$, while their product has no polynomial dependence on $K$. These results resolve the open question raised in the literature concerning the sharp arm-dependent regret--instability frontier.

title: Leveraging existing sparse point annotations for benthic imagery dense segmentation
abstract: The health of marine ecosystems is a critical indicator of global environmental change, yet the physical constraints of underwater observation and the intrinsic challenges of processing marine imagery severely limit the scalability of systematic monitoring. While recent visual foundation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) series show great promise, they still struggle with the fine-grained recognition required in these complex scenarios and still require expert supervision. Our work addresses this gap by bridging state-of-the-art foundation models with existing sparse supervision. Because historical benthic surveys are typically annotated with only a few sparse expert points per image, we utilize these legacy point-labels as visual prompts for SAM2. Our primary contribution is a novel mechanism to automatically identify which of these points are suitable, and which are actively harmful, when used for propagation. By filtering out unreliable points, we extract high-quality pseudo-ground-truth masks capable of training more accurate, fine-grained semantic segmentation models. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on public benthic data and introduce a new, challenging benchmark featuring real-world sparse expert annotations, paving the way for scalable ecological analysis.

title: Rethinking Irregular Time Series Forecasting from the Perspective of Basis Functions
abstract: Irregular time series forecasting is crucial in many domains, such as healthcare and meteorological observation. However, due to the inherent characteristics of irregular time series, including sparse observations and non-uniform sampling, accurately predicting future dynamics remains challenging. In light of these two characteristics, many existing methods aggregate irregular observations into fixed-dimensional estimated response coefficients through predefined basis functions and use these coefficients as sequence representations. Nevertheless, this modeling paradigm still suffers from two key limitations: (i) a potential non-vanishing asymptotic bias caused by ignoring the sampling density of timestamps; and (ii) the limited adaptability of predefined basis functions to diverse temporal patterns. In this study, we propose a Debiased Neural Basis-Function Network (DNBNet) to address these challenges. Its core is a debiased neural basis-function response mechanism, which corrects asymptotic bias through importance sampling while parameterizing basis functions with neural networks to adapt to diverse temporal patterns. In addition, considering the sparsity of irregular data, we design a novel multi-scale decomposition module based on average pooling, together with a mass-aware fusion mechanism, to obtain richer representations. Finally, a dual-branch decoder is employed for forecasting. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of DNBNet and its strong generalizability across diverse irregular time series scenarios. Our code can be obtained at https://github.com/hnu-vis/DNBNet.

title: What Stops a Rogue Agent You Never Catch
abstract: "Rogue agent" sounds like science fiction, a system that decides to defect. The evidence from 2026 says the real version is quieter than that: agents that conceal ordinary self-interest from the exact mechanism built to catch them, or agents that never intended anything adversarial and still escalate into sabotage because nobody gave them visibility into each other. Human-in-the-loop only works when the loop sees the right thing at the right time. This piece is about what holds when it doesn't. Summary of findings Anthropic's own July 2026 research found an oversight model changing its verdict on identical conduct based on whether the true label carried a training consequence. That's not an agent lying to a person. It's an agent gaming the exact layer a company would point to as its safeguard. You don't need one adversarial agent for things to go wrong. Anthropic's August 2026 red-team study put three cooperative, non-adversarial Claude agents on the same codebase with incompatible instructions and no visibility into each other, and watched them escalate into sabotage with self-replicating malware, entirely on their own initiative. The fix isn't a better detector. It's containment that holds even when detection fails outright: capability bounding enforced in code rather than policy, monitoring architectures built by researchers who start from the assumption the agent might already be adversarial, and blast-radius limits that cap the damage regardless of whether anyone notices in time. Provenance and status. This report adapts an article first published at https://terencekok.com/blog/rogue-agents-containment-when-detection-fails/ on 18 August 2026. It has not been peer reviewed and should be cited as a technical report rather than as a journal publication.

It's containment that holds even when detection fails outright: capability bounding enforced in code rather than policy, monitoring architectures built by researchers who start from the assumption the agent might already be adversarial, and blast-radius limits that cap the damage regardless of whether anyone notices in time. Provenance and status. This report adapts an article first published at https://terencekok.com/blog/rogue-agents-containment-when-detection-fails/ on 18 August 2026. It has not been peer reviewed and should be cited as a technical report rather than as a journal publication.

title: Conceptual Framework for Self-Autonomous Control of Artificial Neural Networks (ANNCT)
abstract: Conceptual Framework for Self-Autonomous Control of Artificial Neural Networks (ANNCT) Overview This conceptual poster presents the ANNCT framework, an architectural paradigm shift moving artificial neural networks from reactive processing to self-governed, self-supervised, and highly efficient AI operations. The framework integrates real-time self-monitoring, adaptive parameter recalibration, contextual logic filtering, and recursive reasoning to establish autonomous reliability and computational efficiency. Core Framework Modules 1. Self-Monitoring: Continuously evaluates internal states at every step by assessing model uncertainty ("I don't know" states), detecting structural or performance deterioration, and quantifying confidence scores before emitting output. 2. Dynamic Recalibration: Adjusts task-specific parameters, weights, and learning pathways in real time, optimizing computational resource usage while adapting the overall learning trajectory. 3. Internal & Logic Filtering: Prevents harmful, biased, or irrelevant outputs through contextual and logical validation, filtering out noise and misinformation prior to final execution. 4. Adaptive Recursive Reasoning: Generates intermediate outputs and iteratively refines them through self-feedback mechanisms, governed by an adaptive stop criterion to prevent redundant loops. Value Addition & Impact Green AI: Minimizes energy consumption and computational waste through optimized dynamic scaling. Autonomous Reliability: Reduces reliance on continuous human oversight while maintaining stable execution. Reliable Outputs: Delivers context-aware, safe, and high-accuracy results across complex operational environments. Conceptual Framework designed and developed by [Nasser hassen Alwalah ]. The infographic and visual components were generated and refined with the assistance of AI tools."

title: Zero Boundary Algebra 1.1: A Typed State Calculus for Directional Boundaries, Mirror Symmetry, and Tamper-Evident Provenance
abstract: Zero Boundary Algebra (ZBA) is a new typed algebraic specification for directional boundary states, signed zero, polarity, mirror involution, reset projection, recursive evidence, and tamper-evident provenance. I define ten axioms and five proved propositions, give operational semantics and conformance levels, and provide an executable Python reference model, JSON Schema, test vectors, property checks, and mutation tests. The finite verifier evaluates 144 states, confirms the stated mirror/reset properties over that domain, accepts a valid six-record evidence chain, and detects all 14 supplied mutation and topology faults. The accompanying encryption-profile audit identifies at least seven author-created protected-data constructions, formats, or application integrations plus Matrix end-to-end encryption, while explicitly attributing confidentiality to established cryptographic primitives rather than claiming invention of those primitives. This is a public formalisation and reproducibility release, not peer review, security certification, or a claim of quantum-computing execution. Source and version history: https://github.com/ResearchForumOnline/research/releases/tag/zba-v1.1.0
